title: Traffic Thermostat: adaptive canary policy DSL and enforcement engine
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Build a flexible, testable canary policy DSL and enforcement engine (the "Traffic Thermostat") that controls traffic splits, step schedules, shadowing, and automated rollback decisions. The engine should be able to: (1) express multi-step schedules and conditional transitions, (2) enforce guardrails for latency/error/quality deltas, (3) compute dynamic adjustments based on real-time telemetry, (4) run dry-run simulations against historical traffic, and (5) expose audit events for Console and private deployments. This ticket covers spec, a reference implementation in the routing plane, simulation harness integration, and a CI job to validate safe rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Specification document for the Traffic Thermostat DSL reviewed and approved by PM + SRE
Reference enforcement service that can apply step schedule updates to routing key weights via the routing API
Simulation harness can replay 7 days of production traces and produce a rollback recommendation with a risk score
Guardrails (max-step, error-rate-threshold, p95-latency-delta) implemented and configurable via policy
E2E test demonstrates automated rollback when model error-rate increases > 2% over baseline for >= 3 consecutive minutes
Audit events emitted and visible in Console pipeline for a sample canary run
implementation_plan: Write DSL proto: schedule steps, conditions (metric comparisons, statistical tests), and actions (increase, pause, rollback, shadow)
Implement enforcement worker that listens to policy changes and calls routing API to change traffic weights
Integrate metric adapters: latency, error rate, quality delta (from eval service)
Add simulation mode: replay recorder, synthetic failure injection, compute rollback risk score
Add Console UI hooks for viewing policy status and manual override endpoints
Create CI job to run end-to-end simulation on each deploy to the routing worker
progress_updates: 2026-02-02: Draft DSL spec posted to Confluence (link below). Chose step/condition/action model after reviewing previous state machines.
2026-02-15: Prototype enforcement worker that can move weights for a demo routing key; integration tests added; initial PR opened (GH-Redwood/routing#1812).
2026-02-28: Simulation harness integrated with prod-like trace replay; observed ~70% accuracy on predicting p95 regressions when using quality-delta signal.
2026-03-05: Security requested an SSO-scoped auditing flow for policy updates — added to scope and raised dependency ENG-65990.
2026-03-10: SRE reviewed guardrail thresholds; recommended default max-step 15% and a 2-minute cool-down between step increases.
2026-03-12: Performance test: enforcement worker can apply a weight update to 1000 routing keys within 45s; still need to optimize parallelism.
2026-03-13: PM sign-off on acceptance criteria draft; moving to implementation of automated rollback logic.
blockers: Need a stable hook from the eval service to surface per-request quality deltas (dependency ENG-65012).
RBAC/audit API for private deployments pending security sign-off (ENG-65990).
Routing API rate limits require bump for large-scale enforcement (coord with infra team).
decisions: Use a declarative DSL instead of imperative scripts to make policies auditable and portable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Default guardrail thresholds will be conservative (max-step 15%, cool-down 2m) and exposed as editable policy attributes.
Rollback condition will use a composite signal: sustained error-rate delta + p95 latency regression OR large negative quality-delta from evals.
Simulation risk score formula will weight customer-facing error rate highest, then latency, then quality-delta; thresholds tuned via offline replay.
risks: False positives: overly-sensitive guardrails could rollback healthy models — mitigation: require sustained signal across time window and multiple metrics.
Operational overhead: frequent small steps could create noise; mitigation: cool-down and adaptive step-sizing in the thermostat algorithm.
Data availability: quality-delta depends on eval feedback; for customers without evals, fallback to latency/error heuristics.
notes: This ticket deliberately keeps policy language small — future work will add canary-A/B pooling semantics and weighted experiment cohorts.
Consider adding a shadowing-only mode to collect metrics without affecting production traffic; helpful for model warmup and token cache priming.
Coordination needed with Console team to surface a "Stop Canary" button and to surface audit trail per-routing key.
